opportunities.title: Henry Moore Grants

amount.raw: New Projects and Commissions max £20,000; Acquisitions and Collections max £20,000; Conferences, Lectures and Publications max £5,000; Long-Term Research grants max £20,000; Research and Travel grants max £2,500

opportunities.eligibility_summary: UK and international non-profit organisations (established and operating non-profit for at least 12 months) for all categories except Research and Travel, which is open to individual sculpture historians, academics and conservators researching and publishing on sculpture. Applications to inform/develop an artist's own practice are not accepted.
opportunities.summary: Henry Moore Grants support the growth and development of sculpture across historical, modern and contemporary registers, and fund research expanding the appreciation of sculpture. Categories cover exhibitions, exhibition catalogues, commissions, acquisitions, conservation, cataloguing, display, conferences, lectures, non-commercial publications, long-term research, and research/travel. Applications are considered four times per year via Flexi-Grant.

opportunities.title: Visiting Research Fellowships

amount.raw: Expenses allocation: UK up to £600, Europe up to £700, Rest of world up to £1,000, plus accommodation provided in Leeds or Hertfordshire

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Academics or curators working on historic and contemporary sculpture (Visiting Research Fellowships), artists developing practice through research (Artist Research Fellowships), and established scholars for longer six-week Senior Fellowships. Studio facilities are not offered.
opportunities.summary: Fellowships allow researchers to spend a month using the Henry Moore Institute facilities in Leeds or Henry Moore Studios & Gardens in Hertfordshire, including accommodation, travel and subsistence expenses. Applications were closed for 2026/27 and the next round opens in spring 2027.

opportunities.title: Dissertation Prize

amount.raw: BA dissertation £250 and MA dissertation £250 cash prize; winners also receive Henry Moore Institute publications to the value of £50 and copies of dissertations added to the Research Library

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Open to BA and MA students of all disciplines with a dissertation submitted within the past academic year at a UK university, on sculpture in the broadest sense. Dissertations must not have been previously published.
opportunities.summary: Each year the Henry Moore Institute awards two prizes for extended pieces of writing on contemporary, modern or historical sculpture, for BA and MA dissertations. Submissions for the 2026 prize will open in autumn.
